title: Derived direct image commutes with restriction to opens
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] (more generally of ringed spaces). Let $V\subseteq Y$ be open, put $U=f^{-1}(V)$ and let $g:U\to V$ be the induced morphism. Then for every $E$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] there is a canonical isomorphism $(Rf_*E)|_V\cong Rg_*(E|_U)$ in $D(\mathcal O_V)$, natural in $E$, with $Rf_*$, $Rg_*$ the derived direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image].

source.place: Lemma lemma-restrict-direct-image-open (Tag 08FE), line 7901; proof via Lemma 08BS (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open)

proof.text: Restriction over U=f^{-1}(V) preserves K-injective complexes by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]. Transport this through Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U, whose functor is an additive equivalence and hence preserves K-injective complexes. Use Functor.preservesKInjectiveComplexes_comp to obtain the same property for the full restriction functor from modules on X to modules on the open subscheme U. Both restriction functors are exact (finite limits and colimits are preserved).

source.place: Tag 08BS, as used in the proof of Tag 08FE

proof.text: Construct the underived natural isomorphism f_* followed by restriction to V is isomorphic to restriction to U followed by g_*. Transport both restrictions to Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor using Scheme.Modules.overFunctorEquiv. Compose the pushforwards with SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp. The inverse-image opens agree by image_morphismRestrict_preimage; use the corresponding eqToIso as a natural isomorphism of indexing functors. The scalar-action morphisms agree by morphismRestrict_app (and Opens.ι_appIso). SheafOfModules.pushforwardCongr₂ supplies the natural module-sheaf isomorphism. This is the sectionwise identity M(f^{-1}W) on every open W of V, including the empty open.

proof.text: The derived direct images [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] are moduleDirectImage.rightDerivedFunctor. For arbitrary additive F and exact G, Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso identifies R(F composed with G) with RF followed by G.mapDerivedCategory, so apply its inverse to f_* and restriction on Y. Derive the underived isomorphism of step 2 with Functor.rightDerivedFunctorNatIso. Then Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompIso identifies the right-hand composite using K-injective preservation from step 1. Finally replace the right derived restriction on X by levelwise restriction with rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory and whisker by Rg_*. Composing these four natural isomorphisms gives the required functor isomorphism, with the four derived-category universe levels explicitly retained. All generic derived-functor isomorphisms used here are already proved in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.Comp and .MapDerivedCategory.
